newsitem.title: CROATIA: Bill volume rises at Croatia cent bank auction.
newsitem.headline: Bill volume rises at Croatia cent bank auction.

text.p: The volume of bills sold at Croatia's central bank primary bill auction on Wednesday rose to 118 million kuna ($18.5 million) from 96 million last week as the banking sector enjoyed good liquidity throughout the week.

The accepted rates for 35- and 91-day liquidity bills were unchanged at 7.0 and 8.5 percent, respectively. The bank received no bids for its longest maturity 182-day bills again. Full results on page NBHT.
The net decrease in outstanding central bank paper was 32.8 million kuna, a bank official said.

Participation at primary sales of the central bank paper is limited to Croatia's banking sector which uses these bills as collateral for Lombard loans, granted for a total of 12 working days each month.
The bank official said all Lombard loans had been repaid and no new were sought.
